text:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a consistent ~10-14% tail latency delta between A100s in us-west-2 (AWS) and europe-west1 (GCP) for the same CUDA/driver combo when running quantized Llama2-13b @ seq512, batch=1. not noisy single-run, reproducible across 3 nodes.

aj: any difference in power/clock governors or BIOS between clouds? sometimes cloud images ship in ‘adaptive’ vs ‘performance’.

maria: good call. checked clocks: AWS nodes show sustained 1.35GHz on SM, GCP ones sit at 1.17GHz under same load. we saw higher power limit on aws (300W) vs gcp (250W).

sam: interesting. what about kernel / iommu / cgroup settings? and are the nodes using the same NV driver + CUDA runtime?

maria: driver + cuda: NV 535.113.01 / CUDA 12.3 on both. kernel differs: AWS = 6.4.xx, GCP = 5.15.xx. IOMMU off on both.

linda: could be scheduler + kernel power mgmt. also ask if vulkan/GL stuff loaded? some images have nvidia-persistenced running different flags.

maria: checked persistence: identical. UIDLE governors matched. But nsys traces show more cudaMemcpy stall time on GCP. snippet: ```nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx -o run1 ./bench_runner``` then aggregated timeline shows longer memcpy gaps between kernels on GCP (flat idle gaps ~1.2ms).

perf-bot: autotune suggestion: try setting CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and explicit NV_CUDNN_FRONTEND_TENSOR_CORE=1, and disable MIG if present. Also test with `nvidia-smi -pm 1` and `--application-clocks` pinned.

aj: also verify cpu <-> gpu affinity. if the NVLINK/NUMA topology differs, driver might be scheduling transfers over a different PCIe root complex. run `nvidia-smi topo -m` and `lscpu` to compare.

maria: did topo; AWS nodes have GPU closest to CPU socket0, GCP attaches across a pcie switch to socket1 for that instance type. suspect cross-socket DMA causing memcpy penalty.

sam: that would explain memcpy gaps. for tail latency, a few extra memcpy hops are expensive. can you rebind process to socket1 and retest? also try `cudaMemcpyAsync` vs sync patterns in the runtime.

maria: rebind helped — moving process to the CPU socket nearer the GPU reduced tail ~9% and removed the 1.2ms gaps. reproduces across runs.

linda: for quantized runs, we also care about kernel selection: cudnn conv heuristic picks different kernels when workspace/blas libs differ. confirm cuBLAS/cuDNN patch levels. sometimes distro packaging pulls in older cuDNN.

maria: cuDNN versions identical per `nvcc --version` and `dpkg -l | grep cudnn` but the packaged libcudnn.so symlink target differed (minor build). I'll snapshot both and send.

perf-bot: quick checklist for cross-cloud parity: 1) application clocks pinned 2) GPU <-> CPU NUMA binding 3) same kernel version or tuned preemption settings 4) PCIe ASPM disabled 5) identical driver/cudnn/cuBLAS build IDs.

aj: are you seeing any throughput differences for higher batch sizes, or is it primarily single-stream tail latency?

maria: throughput (batch=8) is similar ±3%. problem is single-stream tail p95/p99 which matters for prod. batch-friendly workloads mask the memcpy scheduling overhead.

sam: for rollout: we should add a small platform check in our onboarding script that validates NUMA affinity and reports `nvidia-smi topo -m`, kernel version, and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=clocks.gr,clocks.sm --format=csv`. If mismatch, recommend `taskset` pinning + application clocks.

linda: also add an opt-in flag to our quantization harness that flips to `interleaved memcpy + async kernel launches` to mitigate gaps. note: increases code complexity but helps tail latency.

maria: will open a tiny PR with the script + the perf-repro recipe and attach the two nsys traces. for now mitigation: pin app to socket near GPU + `nvidia-smi -ac 1215,1410` (example clocks) brought p99 back in line.

ops-bot: alert recorded: "cross-cloud a100 tail-latency — NUMA/clock mismatch". ticket #INF-4982 created and linked to this thread.

aj: perfect. can you include exact node types + AMI/container images in the PR so infra can reproduce and we can add to our onboarding docs?

maria: yes — AWS p4d.24xlarge-like image, GCP a2-highgpu-1g-like; container: rwl-infer:2026-03-15; kernel diffs + nsys traces attached in PR.

sam: one last note — if customers report regional p99 deltas, start by asking for `nvidia-smi topo -m` and `lscpu` before asking for traces. saves time. :thumbsup:

maria: agreed. thanks all. closing for now, will link PR once created. :slightly_smiling_face:
